board.name: Missouri State Board of Registration for the Healing Arts (Advisory Commission for Physician Assistants)

ce.reason: A Missouri physician assistant is by statute a person with active NCCPA certification; no state CME hour count was found.

agreement.text: Before practicing, a PA informs the Board in writing of the collaborating physician. The written collaborative practice arrangement is reviewed at least annually, changes are reported within 15 days, and at least 10% of the PA's charts go to the collaborating physician every 14 days.

unverified: How often the PA license renews (the statute says valid for two years and renewable annually; the board mails renewals every year)
Whether RN renewal requires any continuing education (the renewal rule lists only the fee and workforce data)

ce.reason: Renewal requires primary source evidence of recertification by an approved certifying body before the license expires; no state hour count for certified APRNs.

cycleYears.reason: APRN and RN licenses renew biennially in odd-numbered years.

notes.text: APRNs approved as noncertified before January 1, 2010 instead need 800 practice hours and 60 contact hours every 2 years.
The APRN license expires on the earlier of the RN license expiration and your national certification expiration; renew the certification before it lapses.

agreement.text: APRN practice requires a written collaborative practice arrangement with a physician, reviewed at least annually and not filed with the Board of Nursing. The collaborating physician reviews at least 10% of services every 14 days, and a new arrangement starts with one month of practice with the physician continuously present, with listed exceptions.
